1	# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations
2	
3	What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
4	hang, or crash on a real workload. Written 2026-05-28 from a direct read of
5	the current code (not just the older audit notes).
6	
7	How this file relates to the others:
8	
9	- `docs/TODO.md` - the engineering fix backlog (failure modes `F-T*`). It is
10	  the *plan to fix*. This file is the *plain-English "do not do this" list*.
11	- `ROADMAP.md` - feature roadmap. Its bug-audit wave `B1-B20` is fully closed,
12	  so those are NOT limitations anymore. The open items live in `docs/TODO.md`.
13	
14	Each entry below was checked against the code on 2026-05-28. The `Where`
15	line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow
20	
21	This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
22	consequence of it.
23	
24	When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
25	part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
26	FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
27	`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
28	`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.
29	
30	So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
31	be:
32	
33	- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
34	- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
35	- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
36	- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
37	- No system calls / semihosting
38	- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
39	- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)
40	
41	If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
42	wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload
47	
48	### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)
49	
50	- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
51	  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
52	- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
53	  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
54	  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
55	  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
56	- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
57	  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
58	- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 / phase 3 (the two QEMU
59	  legs). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.
60	
61	### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)
62	
63	- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
64	  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
65	- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
66	  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
67	  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
68	  silently disappears. (PMP IS restored to QEMU2 afterward, so the gap is
69	  the vsim window only.)
70	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
71	- Status: OPEN.
72	
73	### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI
74	
75	- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
76	  almost anything under an OS.
77	- What happens: `satp` is drained and restored to QEMU2, but the resume step
78	  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
79	  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
80	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
81	  `resume()` never writes it.
82	- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
83	  PMP-static but not paging).
84	
85	### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)
86	
87	- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
88	  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
89	- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
90	  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through to QEMU2. Any
91	  trap-diagnostic logic after the handoff sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
92	  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
93	  the ROI starts from reset values.
94	- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
95	  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
96	- Status: OPEN.
97	
98	### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)
99	
100	- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
101	  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
102	- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
103	  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
104	  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
105	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
106	- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
107	  at the trigger.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up
112	
113	### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)
114	
115	- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
116	  trigger boundary.
117	- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
118	  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
119	  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. On the QEMU2 side,
120	  `apply_state` never writes `priv` at all (it is in the struct at
121	  `abi.py:37` but absent from `gdbstub.py:271-319`). S/U code then raises
122	  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
123	- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`, `gdbstub.py` apply_state.
124	- Status: OPEN.
125	
126	### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)
127	
128	- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
129	  shared memory.
130	- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
131	  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
132	  corruption.
133	- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
134	  ELF size against it.
135	- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.
136	
137	### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)
138	
139	- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
140	  sync.
141	- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
142	  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
143	  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
144	  both.
145	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
146	  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
147	- Status: OPEN.
148	
149	### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)
150	
151	- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
152	  any aliased/device memory.
153	- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
154	  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory. QEMU2
155	  device state then disagrees with vsim.
156	- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
157	- Status: OPEN.
158	
159	---
160	
161	## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits
162	
163	### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU
164	
165	- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
166	  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
167	- What happens: the QEMU2 spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
168	  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
169	  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
170	  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
171	  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
172	  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
173	  these per machine.
174	- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
175	- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.
176	
177	### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)
178	
179	- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
180	  or any future config change to VLEN.
181	- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
182	  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
183	  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
184	  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
185	  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
186	  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
187	- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
188	- Status: OPEN.
189	
190	### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0
191	
192	- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
193	  immediate 0 or 1.
194	- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
195	  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
196	  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
197	  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
198	- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
199	- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.
200	
201	### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)
202	
203	- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
204	- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
205	  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
206	  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
207	  this gate must change together.
208	- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
209	- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.
210	
211	### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement
212	
213	- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim estimate` run where you read
214	  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
215	- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
216	  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
217	  (`hsim:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
218	  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
219	  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
220	     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
221	     CPI is biased high.
222	  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
223	     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
224	- Where: `hsim:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
225	- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.
226	
227	---
228	
229	## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps
230	
231	### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)
232	
233	- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
234	  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
235	- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
236	  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
237	  against the drained state.
238	- Where: `hsim` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
239	- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see TODO.md "next moves").
240	
241	### L16. CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name
242	
243	- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
244	  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
245	- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
246	  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
247	  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
248	  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
249	- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
250	- Status: OPEN.
251	
252	### L17. gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick
253	
254	- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
255	  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
256	- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
257	  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
258	  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
259	  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
260	  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
261	- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
262	- Status: OPEN.
263	
264	### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only
265	
266	- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
267	  with different struct alignment.
268	- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
269	  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
270	  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
271	  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
272	- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
273	- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).
274	
275	### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)
276	
277	- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
278	  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
279	- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
280	  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
281	- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
282	  mid-run are not covered.
283	- A QEMU2 that launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a
284	  zombie (no SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
285	- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.
286	
287	---
288	
289	## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)
290	
291	`CLAUDE.md` and parts of the architecture notes still describe
292	`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` as the component that spawns QEMU2
293	and sends gdbstub P-packets. That file no longer exists - the QEMU2 spawn and
294	handback moved into the Python orchestrator (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` +
295	`gdbstub.py`) in commit `7c7bf30`. Anyone debugging the handback by following
296	the docs will look in the wrong place.
297	
298	---
299	
300	## Quick reference
301	
302	| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
303	|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
304	| L1  | No syscalls/semihosting in ROI          | blocker  | open   |

306	| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
307	| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |

309	| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | open   |

part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No system calls / semihosting
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

---

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 / phase 3 (the two QEMU
  legs). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears. (PMP IS restored to QEMU2 afterward, so the gap is
  the vsim window only.)
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained and restored to QEMU2, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
  PMP-static but not paging).

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through to QEMU2. Any
  trap-diagnostic logic after the handoff sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
  the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

---

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
  trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. On the QEMU2 side,
  `apply_state` never writes `priv` at all (it is in the struct at
  `abi.py:37` but absent from `gdbstub.py:271-319`). S/U code then raises
  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`, `gdbstub.py` apply_state.
- Status: OPEN.

### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
  shared memory.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption.
- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
  ELF size against it.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
  any aliased/device memory.
- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory. QEMU2
  device state then disagrees with vsim.
- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
- Status: OPEN.

---

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
- What happens: the QEMU2 spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
  these per machine.
- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.

### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
  or any future config change to VLEN.
- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0

- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
  immediate 0 or 1.
- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.

### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)

- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
  this gate must change together.
- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim estimate` run where you read
  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
  (`hsim:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
     CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

---

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
  against the drained state.
- Where: `hsim` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see TODO.md "next moves").

### L16. CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name

- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L17. gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick

- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
  with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- A QEMU2 that launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a
  zombie (no SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

---

## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

`CLAUDE.md` and parts of the architecture notes still describe
`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` as the component that spawns QEMU2
and sends gdbstub P-packets. That file no longer exists - the QEMU2 spawn and

No. Today hsim moves a fixed, narrow slice of state, and the design as written cannot reach "all CSRs + all arch state" without a new wire version and lifting the ROI rules. Details:

## What it actually carries today

Fixed list in `state_abi.h` (the only state that round-trips):
- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch, medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`

## What is missing right now

- **All S-mode / U-mode CSRs**: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip, scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp` - none exist in the struct.
- **`fcsr` / `frm` / `fflags`** - absent. FP rounding mode is not carried, so non-default rounding before the ROI gives wrong FP results. (Concrete gap even inside the "standard" set.)
- **HPM counters** (`mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`), `mcounteren, menvcfg, mcountinhibit, misa, time`.
- **Every Andes-custom CSR** (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause`, ...). Zero are transported. Worse, Andes CSR `0x7C0` is *repurposed* as the trigger marker, not preserved.
- **Carried but NOT restored into vsim**: `satp, mepc, mcause, mtval, mscratch, medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP. `resume_driver.hpp:60-145` writes back only 4 CSRs (`mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret`) + GPR/FPR/V. So even state in the struct does not enter the measured region (this is limitations L2/L3/L4).

## Why "all" is hard by design

There are 4 transport surfaces, each with its own ceiling:

| Surface | Mechanism | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| QEMU1 drain | plugin reads by **name** from gdbstub XML | can only drain CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer, by **number** | most general; but cannot write RO/WARL/locked CSRs to arbitrary bits |
| vsim drain | DMI Abstract read, by **number** | general for readable CSRs |
| QEMU2 handback | gdbstub P-packet by **name** | silently skips any CSR the stub doesn't name (L16); you already had to patch QEMU for `vl/vtype` [[project_qemu_vl_vtype]] |

Two structural blockers:
1. **Wire format**: `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64`. Fine for a handful more CSRs, but the meaningful M+S+U+HPM+Andes set far exceeds that. "All" needs a v2 / variable layout.
2. **Semantics, not just bits**: restore order and side effects already bite (mstatus.FS/VS gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for vtype/vl). Side-effecting CSRs - `satp` (TLB flush), Andes `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` (cache/prefetch/BP enable) - may be RO/locked or not replay correctly when written via the debug module mid-run. And those Andes microarch CSRs are exactly the ones that *matter for cycle accuracy* in vsim.

Bottom line: the design is intentionally scoped to an M-mode, bare, trap-free ROI. Extending to a larger but bounded CSR set (add S-mode + `fcsr` + a chosen Andes subset to v2, restore them in vsim) is feasible. "All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without a redesign of the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

Want me to scope a v2 that adds the highest-value missing ones (`fcsr`, S-mode trap CSRs, and the Andes microarch CSRs that affect cycles)?

**Rating: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal/research tool for its narrow design envelope.**

Honest scorecard:

| Axis | Score | Note |
|------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity      | 8/10 | Three-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline    | 7/10 | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, candid `limitation.md`. |
| State coverage (correctness surface) | 3/10 | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload    | 2/10 | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls. |
| ISA completeness          | 3/10 | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (and the vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility | 4/10 | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors       | 5/10 | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed, with only a diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding         | 7/10 | CLAUDE.md, USER_GUIDE.md, limitation.md are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures             | 6/10 | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
| Portability               | 4/10 | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed; pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

What blocks commercial shipping:

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically fine but be wrong (L20). `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore is observable only through a private counter.
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging, no syscalls inside the window" rules out every real OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything with page faults.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport is a credibility hit (L21).
4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`, `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into vsim - they exist in the wire format but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond the three FLAG bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** podman-required vsim build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts, `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a commercial CI matrix.

What it does well (and why the 7/10 internal-tool score):

- The three-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (limitation.md with 21 entries plus a state-coverage section) rather than hiding it. Commercially, that document would be the release-blocker checklist; internally, it is exemplary engineering honesty.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation is a real differentiator.

Bottom line: ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial release you need v2 wire format, S-mode + traps inside ROI, Andes vendor CSR transport, fcsr fix, and a proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing. That is roughly a 6-9 month hardening track, not weeks.
